label: August 1915
atlas_dek: The episodes of anti-Black violence reported in August 1915 from our dossiers, placed on 1915 county lines and by month (some July events were first reported in August). Hover for a short summary; select a dot to read the account in the sidebar. Drafts: no entry has had human review.
reader_intro:
Dossiers for 39 episodes of anti-Black violence reported in August 1915. They come from the August 1915 table, which includes July events first reported in August, among them the mob hunt for Joe Deberry at Murphysboro, Illinois, plus three events found by later checks of every August article for peonage and for attacks by one person. We did not write dossiers for two lynchings of white victims (Leo Frank at Marietta, Georgia, and Mary Dennis at Cagle, Tennessee) or for twelve events that belong to other months, among them the burning of Will Stanley at Temple, Texas, on July 31 and police killings that an Alexandria paper recalled from decades earlier. Searches covered August papers, plus September papers for more on known episodes.

Twenty-one of the 60 dossiers are set aside. One is a duplicate: an editorial’s “burning at Tampa” is a garbled report of the Temple burning. Five belong to other months, including night-rider raids near Stuttgart, Arkansas, some time before late July, the July 31 raid on Island 37 near Osceola, Arkansas, in which a sheriff’s posse fatally wounded Bert Spring, and the threats against Wish Sheppard during his July trial at Denton, Maryland. Fifteen are out of scope. Andy Crum, shot in the Osceola jail on August 12, was white. Starkville, Mississippi, held a legal public hanging, and the lynching of Charles Robinson in Abbeville County, South Carolina, was a false report. No report gives anyone’s race in two cases, and in two others the attackers were Black. Three manhunts harmed no Black person, two fights were two-sided, and three cases involved no force: a strike threat at Bayonne, New Jersey, and two police removals.

Police violence is kept generously: men shot while fleeing or resisting arrest are included, and only gunfights over a crime in progress are set aside from the totals. Peonage, force used to hold a Black worker to labor, is always included, even when one employer acted alone. Where an inventory’s race differs from the press, the entry keeps the inventory and states the difference.

Attacks by one person: our definition covers violence by groups and by people acting with public authority, so an attack by a single private person is normally left out. A check of every August article for such attacks added the Coffee County, Alabama, peonage case and the killing of Irene Hawkins, a Black chambermaid, at a Nashville hotel, both kept and marked as one-person attacks. A shooting at Pass Creek, Wyoming, proved two-sided.

Method: a research agent (Sonnet) searched Black and white papers. A write-up agent (Opus) wrote the dossier with keyed citations, and a code check confirmed every quote and citation against the article text. Black-press clippings are shown as page images; white-press clippings are page images where we could place them on the scan, otherwise text.

Drafts: no entry has had human review.
